rev2026.label: 2026 model revenue
rev2026.definition: Illustrative full-year revenue in USD billions. Actual-period revenue and annualized pace remain separate observations.

g1.label: 2027–2030 annual growth
g1.definition: Revenue growth applied in each of the four years from 2027 through 2030.

g2.label: 2031–2033 annual growth
g2.definition: Revenue growth applied in each of the three years from 2031 through 2033.

g3.label: 2034–2036 annual growth
g3.definition: Revenue growth applied in the final three forecast years, before the terminal period begins.
g3.limit: 0% to 200%; no lower than perpetual growth.

m27.label: 2027 EBIT margin
m27.definition: Operating profit as a share of revenue. Annual margins interpolate between the 2027, 2030 and 2036 anchors.

m30.label: 2030 EBIT margin
m30.definition: The middle operating-margin anchor. Tax applies only when EBIT is positive.

m36.label: 2036 EBIT margin
m36.definition: The final explicit and terminal EBIT margin. Changing this also changes the interpolated margin path for 2031–2036.

turns.label: Sales / invested capital
turns.definition: Incremental revenue divided by net reinvestment. Reinvestment includes net capital expenditure and working capital.

wacc.label: Cost of capital
wacc.definition: The weighted average cost of capital discounts the remaining-2026 cash flow, all explicit forecast cash flows and terminal value.
wacc.limit: Above perpetual growth and no more than 60%.

tg.label: Perpetual growth
tg.definition: Annual growth after 2036. The terminal reinvestment rate equals perpetual growth divided by terminal ROIC.
tg.limit: At least 0%; below both WACC and terminal ROIC, and no higher than 2034–2036 growth.

roic.label: Terminal ROIC
roic.definition: Return on invested capital in the terminal period. It determines the reinvestment needed to support perpetual growth.
roic.limit: Above perpetual growth and no more than 100%.

stub.label: Remaining-2026 FCFF
stub.definition: Free cash flow to the firm from 18 October through 31 December 2026. Negative values are outflows; this cash flow is included once.

tax.label: Tax on positive EBIT
tax.definition: Tax on positive operating profit. The model provides no loss benefit or tax-loss carryforward.

facts.modelImplication: Use $965B as dated completed post-money equity benchmark. Do not re-add $15B prior commitments or the included $5B Amazon investment.
Use $852B completed post-money equity benchmark. $122B is committed capital; $4.7B facility was undrawn at close and is not debt outstanding.
Keep separate from completed rounds. Mechanical post-money would be at least $1,430B if unchanged terms close; this is arithmetic, not a reported completed valuation.
Scenario reference only. Neither amount replaces the completed $965B financing benchmark.
Historical pace metric. Do not enter as FY2026 actual revenue.
A $24B annualized equivalent is derived arithmetic, not FY2026 revenue.

facts.metric: Latest directly retrieved reported monthly run-rate
facts.modelImplication: Label July observation separately from August publication. Later Q3 actual-period reporting is more recent evidence.
Supersedes earlier near-$70B comparison claim. This is a metric-basis correction, not proof revenue declined.
Use $11.6B Q2 when using this latest report; earlier Reuters used $11.5B. Adjusted profitability is not GAAP EBIT or free cash flow.
Do not align this older quarter with Anthropic Q3 as a same-period comparison.
Net loss is not cash burn; financing remeasurement dominates. December liquidity cannot be used as an October cash balance.
Keep annual realized revenue separate from exit run-rate. Training/R&D and serving costs must both be covered in modeled operating cash flows.
Fees are reported in sales/marketing/partnerships expense. The ~16% fee applies to channel sales, not all revenue. Gross margin and revenue multiples need common definitions.

value.openai_to_microsoft_revenue_share: continues through 2030 at same percentage, total cap

facts.modelImplication: Do not carry old reciprocal royalties or exclusivity into forecast. Percentage and cap are not disclosed in this primary summary.
Separate equity financing inflow from operating/capacity spending. Initial $5B is included in Series H, not incremental to it.
No assumption all announced investments are current cash. Do not classify $138B aggregate nominal service commitments as borrowing.
Mixed service floors, leases and cancelable capacity. Do not subtract $518B from EV as debt; schedule relevant costs and avoid double counting existing forecast expense.
Debt is described as backed by Anthropic leases; borrower/recourse/closing unknown. No addition to direct corporate debt without documentation.
Use as a funding-needs stress case, not cash burn already incurred or disclosed guidance. $350B is a reported 2030 projection.

contexts.title: Revenue periods and annualized pace
contexts.summary: The snapshot records company-announced and reported annualized revenue alongside reported quarterly revenue. Each observation retains its own measurement period and accounting context.
contexts.limitation: Annualized pace is not full-year revenue. The observations do not establish any of the future annual growth rates in the selected case.

contexts.title: The published Base revenue construction
contexts.summary: The frozen Base construction combines reported Q1–Q3 revenue of $33.1B with illustrative Q4 revenue of $20.16B, giving $53.26B. This explains the published Base input; the current case value is shown separately above.
contexts.limitation: S18 supplies the reported quarterly components, not the Q4 assumption or a reported full-year actual. An edited or different preset value remains an analyst or user assumption.

contexts.title: Operating costs and partner accounting
contexts.summary: Reported historical financials and cloud-channel fees provide context for the costs that future operating margins must cover. The investor-day report also describes adjusted profitability.
contexts.limitation: Adjusted profitability is not disclosed GAAP EBIT or free cash flow. The channel fee analysis applies to channel sales, and none of these observations establishes the selected future EBIT margins.

contexts.title: Compute capacity and capital requirements
contexts.summary: The snapshot separates an announced investment and compute agreement, reported infrastructure obligations, and a reported chip-financing proposal. These commitments help frame questions about the capital needed for growth.
contexts.limitation: Nominal service commitments, leases and proposed financing do not directly determine sales-to-capital turns or terminal ROIC. Payment schedules and accounting treatment remain incomplete; avoid counting costs already captured in forecast expenses or reinvestment twice.

contexts.title: Financing references and investor rights
contexts.summary: The completed financing, reported IPO expectations and published Trust structure describe different aspects of financing and control. They are dated context for an independent valuation.
contexts.limitation: An equity valuation headline or governance right does not establish WACC. Current net cash, security preferences and a complete economic ownership bridge remain unavailable; the selected discount rate is an assumption.

contexts.title: A remaining-period cash-flow assumption
contexts.summary: The model values the remaining portion of 2026 through a separate cash-flow input. Historical financials and multi-year infrastructure obligations help identify why current cash-flow information would matter.
contexts.limitation: Neither historical net loss nor nominal multi-year commitments establish FCFF from 18 October through 31 December 2026. The selected stub is illustrative and is included once in the model.

contexts.title: Growth requires terminal reinvestment
contexts.summary: The terminal reinvestment rate is perpetual growth divided by terminal ROIC. The model uses this relationship when converting terminal operating profit into cash flow and discounting the continuation value.
contexts.limitation: The methodology source supports a relationship, not an Anthropic-specific growth rate, cost of capital or return on capital. The transition from explicit growth and reinvestment into the terminal period remains a modeling choice.

contexts.title: An explicit simplified tax policy
contexts.summary: The selected rate applies only to positive EBIT. The model provides no tax benefit for losses and does not carry tax losses forward.
contexts.limitation: The research snapshot does not establish Anthropic's future cash tax rate or usable tax-loss balances. The default 25% and any edited rate are analyst or user assumptions.

contexts.title: Revenue observations and accounting basis
contexts.summary: The snapshot records company-announced monthly pace, reported September annualized revenue and reported Q2 revenue. These are different measures and measurement periods.
contexts.limitation: The September comparison is a metric-basis correction, not proof of a revenue decline. Monthly or annualized pace does not establish full-year revenue or future growth; accounting changes also require consistent margin and capital treatment.

contexts.title: The published full-year revenue input
contexts.summary: The frozen Base case retains the illustrative $35B full-year revenue input from the earlier model. The current selected case may use a different value.
contexts.limitation: The retained input is not a verified company forecast or reported FY2026 actual. Related reporting is context and does not convert this input into a company disclosure.

contexts.title: Operating costs and commercial terms
contexts.summary: Reported historical financials identify serving and research costs. The April 2026 Microsoft agreement summary updates the commercial context that a future margin path must reflect.
contexts.limitation: The primary agreement does not specify the royalty percentage or total cap. Historical operating losses and contract terms do not establish the selected future EBIT margins.

contexts.title: Capacity commitments and reported forecasts
contexts.summary: An announced investment and compute agreement and a reported management presentation describe future capacity and funding needs. The presentation is attributed reporting of a forecast, with partial source access in this snapshot.
contexts.limitation: Committed capital is not necessarily current cash; compute service commitments are not automatically debt. The reported revenue and funding projections do not validate capital turns, future growth or terminal ROIC in the selected case.

contexts.title: Financing terms and historical ownership
contexts.summary: The completed funding round, proposed financing target and historical recapitalization structure describe separate financing and governance observations.
contexts.limitation: Post-money and proposed pre-money equity references are not operating enterprise value or a disclosed discount rate. Historical ownership percentages and conditional capital do not provide a verified current equity bridge.

contexts.title: A remaining-period cash-flow assumption
contexts.summary: The model includes a separate remaining-2026 FCFF input. Historical financial reporting and the reported management cash-flow forecast provide broader funding context.
contexts.limitation: Annual historical operating losses and cumulative multi-year forecast outflows do not establish cash flow for 18 October through 31 December 2026. No current-period cash-flow schedule is reconstructed from these figures.

contexts.title: Growth requires terminal reinvestment
contexts.summary: The terminal reinvestment rate is perpetual growth divided by terminal ROIC. The model uses this relationship when converting terminal operating profit into cash flow and discounting the continuation value.
contexts.limitation: The methodology source supports a relationship, not an OpenAI-specific growth rate, cost of capital or return on capital. The transition from explicit growth and reinvestment into the terminal period remains a modeling choice.

contexts.title: An explicit simplified tax policy
contexts.summary: The selected rate applies only to positive EBIT. The model provides no tax benefit for losses and does not carry tax losses forward.
contexts.limitation: The research snapshot does not establish OpenAI's future cash tax rate or usable tax-loss balances. The default 25% and any edited rate are analyst or user assumptions.
